paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when trouble comes, the question is WHO you trust. Psalm 20 is a whole song of people praying for someone else, one "May the LORD…" after another, and then it turns on a dime with "Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed" (Psalm 20:6). Hoping becomes knowing. That's the move God wants from all of us.

Then comes the line that carries the whole psalm: "Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God" (Psalm 20:7). Chariots and horses are what you can see, count and park in the driveway. Plenty of people lean on that stuff, and I get it, because I leaned on a junk drawer once. But the psalm says those who do "collapse and fall, but we rise up and stand firm" (Psalm 20:8).

So here's what you carry out of my bakery today. Trouble is real, but you don't face it alone, and you don't have to face it with your own strength. Pray for the people around you like this song does, and call on the LORD yourself, because the last line says, "Answer us on the day we call" (Psalm 20:9). Trust Him first, baker, and you'll be standing when the dust settles.
